title: Data Analysis and Trend Identification
tagline: Year 3 — Reading a time series: rises, falls, averages, moving averages, growth and simple forecasts

introduction.overview: A trend is the general direction of a series over time. Data analysis questions ask you to find it and to describe it with numbers: the biggest rise or fall, how many periods were above average, the growth between two periods, a moving average that smooths short-term ups and downs, and a simple forecast that extends the average change. The skill is to compute the right summary and to describe what it says without over-reading.
introduction.placementRelevance: Time-series and trend questions appear in DI sections to test analysis as well as arithmetic.
introduction.realWorldContext: Reading monthly sales, website traffic or temperature records and deciding whether things are rising is everyday analysis.

learningObjectives: Find the period of greatest rise or fall
Compute averages and compare periods with them
Use moving averages and quarterly totals
Make a simple forecast from average change

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Change = later − earlier. Average = total ÷ number of periods. Growth % = change ÷ earlier × 100.

coreDefinitions: Trend: the overall direction of a series.
Period-to-period change: difference between consecutive values.
Moving average: average of a fixed number of consecutive periods.
Seasonality: a repeated pattern within a year.
Forecast: a projection based on past change.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: A trend is the story of the series in one sentence. Compute differences to find the story and averages to summarise it.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: List the changes between consecutive periods. Mark positive and negative ones. The largest and the sign pattern describe the trend.

mainNarrative: Changes between consecutive months (February to December): +12, −4, +17, +15, −5, +15, +15, −5, +20, +15, +15. The largest rise is +20 in October (from 180 in September to 200).
The series dips in March, June and September but rises overall: from 120 in January to 230 in December. The overall growth is (230 − 120) ÷ 120 = 91.7%.
The yearly total is 2,020 and the monthly average is 168.3. Sales were above average in July (170) and in every later month, and below it in all earlier months, so six months were above average.
Quarterly totals smooth monthly noise: 380, 460, 535, 645. Sales rise in every quarter.
A simple forecast uses the average monthly change: (230 − 120) ÷ 11 = 10. If it continues, the next month would be 240.

deepDiveAspects.title: Moving average
deepDiveAspects.content: A three-month moving average removes dips; it makes the upward trend clearer.

deepDiveAspects.title: Forecast limits
deepDiveAspects.content: A forecast assumes the past pattern continues; it is an estimate, not a fact.

solvedExamples.title: Largest rise
solvedExamples.question: Sales were 180 in September and 200 in October; 160 in May and 155 in June. Which month-to-month change is larger?
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: One is a rise, the other a fall.

solvedExamples.title: Moving average
solvedExamples.question: Sales for January, February and March are 120, 132 and 128. What is their three-month average?

solvedExamples.title: Forecast
solvedExamples.question: Sales rose from 120 (January) to 230 (December), 11 steps. What is the average monthly change?

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Write the list of month-to-month changes once; the biggest rise, the dips and the average change all come from that list.

commonMistakes.mistake: Dividing by 12 for the average change

commonMistakes.whyItHappens: A fall is not a rise.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: The average must lie between the minimum and maximum.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Describe the trend in a sentence before computing anything.

selfCheckQuestions: Can I find the biggest rise?
Can I count months above average?
